title: Operationalizing catalog safety & compatibility checklist for customer model intake
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Create a repeatable operational checklist and lightweight gating flow for customer-submitted model additions and variant pins that balances speed for enterprise customers with safety, licensing, and compatibility guarantees. This ticket scopes the checklist, automation hooks, and the reviewer rotation required to operationalize intake for regulated or quantized model requests.
background: Customers increasingly request: pinned quantized variants, licensed third-party models, and fast-track onboarding for regulated workloads. Current ad-hoc reviews cause long lead times and inconsistent outcomes. We need a deterministic intake that enforces license checks, tokenization/embedding compatibility, eval gate thresholds, and audit logging while allowing a sponsored fastpath for high-value customers.
motivation: Reduce time-to-approval for customer model requests from weeks to days for sponsored lanes while reducing incidents from incompatible or non-compliant models. Provide clear SLA for PMs, Sales, and Support on expected review time and required artifacts.
proposed_solution: Deliver a modular checklist and gating playbook that includes: an intake form with mandatory fields, automated triage score (compatibility, license, privacy, perf risk), a minimal automated compatibility test-suite, an eval gate harness template, reviewer runbook for canary rollouts and pinned variants, and a dashboard showing pending requests and bottlenecks. Implement basic automation to block requests that fail license parsing or PII redaction checks.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form published and linked in Console and Partner docs
Automated triage returns a compatibility score for 90% of submissions within 30 minutes
Compatibility test-suite (tokenization, embedding vector dim check, model signature) runs in CI and passes for onboarding requests
Eval gate template with user-defined intent set can be instantiated by PMs and reaches >=80% coverage on sampled intents before canary
Reviewer runbook documented with canary rollout steps, rollback criteria, and escalation paths
SLA for sponsored fastpath defined: 72 hours from complete submission to decision
Telemetry events emitted for audit (who approved, tests run, canary metrics) and visible in Console
decisions: Use triage score buckets (green/yellow/red) to route to fastpath/manual review/deny
Require licence SPDX or distributor attestation for any non-open-source model
Quantized variants must pass numerical-compatibility checks before pin approval
open_questions: What minimum eval suite size do we require for high-risk regulatory customers?
Should we allow temporary pin windows (30/90 days) for fast approval or require permanent pin requests?
What team owns escalations during out-of-hours incidents for canaries?
